questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to do with a brick?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to carve the city of Jerusalem on a brick and then lay siege against it.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to do this with a brick?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to do this as a sign to the house of Israel.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to lie on his left side?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to lie on his left side to carry the sin of the house of Israel.

questions.q: Why was Ezekiel to lie on his left side for 390 days?
questions.a: Ezekiel was to lie on his left side for 390 days to represent 390 years of punishment for the house of Israel.

questions.q: Why was Ezekiel to lie on his right side?
questions.a: Ezekiel was to lie on his right side to carry the sin of the house of Israel.

questions.q: Why was Ezekiel to lie on his right side for 40 days?
questions.a: Ezekiel was to lie on his right side for 40 days to represent 40 years of punishment for the house of Israel.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to eat and drink while he lay on his side?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to eat barley cakes and to drink water.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to eat and drink while he lay on his side?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to eat barley cakes and to drink water.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to bake using human excrement within the sight of the house of Israel?
questions.a: Ezekiel was to bake using human excrement as a sign that the food the people of Israel would eat among the nations would be unclean.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh then allow Ezekiel to use cow dung instead of man’s dung to bake?
questions.a: Yahweh allowed cow dung because Ezekiel had never eaten anything unclean in his life.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would happen in Jerusalem regarding food and drink?
questions.a: Yahweh said that bread and water would be rationed.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would happen to the people of Jerusalem during this time?
questions.a: Yahweh said the people of Jerusalem would be dismayed and would melt away.

commentary.text: The siege of Jerusalem. (Ezek. 4:1-8) The famine the inhabitants would suffer. (Ezek. 4:9-17)

Ezek. 4:1-8 The prophet was to represent the siege of Jerusalem by signs. He was to lie on his left side for a number of days, supposed to be equal to the years from the establishment of idolatry. All that the prophet sets before the children of his people, about the destruction of Jerusalem, is to show that sin is the provoking cause of the ruin of that once flourishing city.

Ezek. 4:9-17 The bread which was Ezekiel's support, was to be made of coarse grain and pulse mixed together, seldom used except in times of urgent scarcity, and of this he was only to take a small quantity. Thus was figured the extremity to which the Jews were to be reduced during the siege and captivity. Ezekiel does not plead, Lord, from my youth I have been brought up delicately, and never used to any thing like this; but that he had been brought up conscientiously, and never had eaten any thing forbidden by the law. It will be comfortable when we are brought to suffer hardships, if our hearts can witness that we have always been careful to keep even from the appearance of evil. See what woful work sin makes, and acknowledge the righteousness of God herein. Their plenty having been abused to luxury and excess, they were justly punished by famine. When men serve not God with cheerfulness in the abundance of all things, God will make them serve their enemies in the want of all things.
